subject.title: Feature: Session authentication PIN gate (framework-level tool blocking)

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in core session PIN gate, and if so what trusted verifier and secret source are acceptable for that auth boundary?
rationale: The request is useful but creates a new framework-level auth, secret-handling, config, and session-state contract that code inspection alone cannot safely choose.

options.title: Design an opt-in core gate first
options.body: Define the threat model, secret source, trusted verifier, reset semantics, and tests before accepting implementation work.

options.title: Keep this as plugin policy
options.body: Document or prototype the behavior through trusted tool policies if maintainers do not want a core auth primitive yet.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Leave current allowlists, approvals, sandboxing, and plugin hooks as the supported hardening path for now.

recommendation.title: Design an opt-in core gate first
recommendation.body: Define the threat model, secret source, trusted verifier, reset semantics, and tests before accepting implementation work.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest combined current-file history signal across the inspected core paths and adjacent auth/session-state work.
